html {
   overflow-y: scroll;
}

body {
   padding: 0;
   margin: 0;
   -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
   font: 13px/1.231 arial, helvetica, clean, sans-serif;
}

body.warn-page {
   background: #ffffcc;
}

#page-container {
   margin: 0;
   padding: 0;
   min-width: 1275px;
}

.kdp-top-header {
   background:
      url("https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/G/01/kindlepubs/common/layouts/nav-bar-bg._V156427298_.png")
      repeat-x scroll 0 0 transparent;
   height: 29px;
}

.header-row {
   background-color: #F5F5F5;
   padding-top: 6px;
   padding-bottom: 3px;
}

.top-links {
   padding: 5px 20px;
   text-align: right;
}

.top-links a, .top-links .language-chooser, .header-item, .header-item .language-chooser {
   margin: 0 10px;
}

.kdp-delim {
   color: #CCCCCC;
}

.language-option {
   font-size: 11px;
}

.language-option a {
   margin: 5px;
}

.language-option .disable {
   color: #666666;
   margin: 0 5px;
}

body .kdp-header {
   color: #004B91;
   height: 95px;
   padding: 35px 0 0 0;
   position: relative;
   text-align: left;
}

.a-lt-ie8 body .kdp-header {
   height: 90px;
}

.tabs {
   color: #004B91;
   font-family: Arial;
   text-decoration: none;
}

.kdp-header .tabs {
   font-size: 16px;
}

.kdp-header .tabs .kdp-delim {
   padding: 0 15px;
}

.kdp-header .tabs .selected {
   font-weight: bold;
}

.account-incomplete {
   margin-top: 1em;
   position: absolute;
   right: 0;
   top: 0;
}

.account-incomplete .a-alert-content {
   font-size: 13px;
   color: #333;
}

.kdp-top-footer {
   background:
      url("https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/G/01/kindlepubs/common/layouts/footer-top._V192549182_.gif")

   height: 23px;
   margin-top: 1em;
}

.social-footer {
   color: #666666;
   text-align: left;
}

.kdp-footer {
   color: #666666;
   text-align: left;
   font-family: Verdana, Geneva, Sans-Serif;
   font-size: 10px;
   margin: 20px 0;
   padding: 0 10px;
   position: relative;
}

.social-footer .links a, .kdp-footer .links a {
   color: #666666;
   text-decoration: underline;
}

.social-footer .links, .kdp-footer .links {
   text-align: center;
}

.kdp-footer .cr, .kdp-footer .kdp-social, .kdp-footer .links {
   padding-top: 10px;
}

.kdp-social a {
   display: inline-block;
}

.kdp-facebook {
   background:
      url("https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/G/01/otp/general/find-us-on-facebook-intl._V142003952_.png")

   cursor: pointer;
   height: 20px;
   margin-right: 10px;
   width: 75px;
}

.en_US .kdp-facebook {
   background:
      url("https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/G/01/otp/general/find-us-on-facebook-a._V151334219_.png")

}

         <span class="breadcrumb active node">
            
            <a id="help-topic-crumb-G202169030" class="a-link-normal" href="/en_US/help/topic/G202169030">Format Images in Your Book</a>
         </span>

               <div id="help-content" class="a-section help-content">
                  






   
   
      
         <div class="a-section a-spacing-large">
            <h2 class="a-spacing-small help-title">
               Format Images in Your Book
            </h2>
            <div class="a-section a-spacing-large help-body">
               <table border="0"><tbody><tr>
<td>For the best results, all images should be sized at 100%, flattened to one layer, and inserted into your manuscript file at a minimum resolution of 300 DPI (dots per inch). Color photos only print in color if you chose a color ink printing option for your book. Black-and-white photos print in black and white no matter whether you choose black or color ink.
<br><br>
Want to preview your paperback or hardcover before making it available to customers? <a href="/help?topicId=G202131440">Order a proof copy</a>.
</td>
<td align="right" width="250">
<img height="20" width="160" src="https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/G/01/15/29/94/76/43/02/15299476430286.png"><br><span class="a-color-tertiary">A paperback manuscript formatting guide</span>
</td>
<td width="190">  <a href="/help?topicId=G202145400"><img height="40" width="175" src="https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/G/01/00/01/21/87/82/06/12187820610.png"></a></td></tr></tbody></table>
<p></p>
<div class="a-span4">
<div class="a-box a-spacing-small a-color-alternate-background">
<div class="a-box-inner">
<h3>Contents</h3>
<hr>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/G202169030#tips">Top tips for formatting images in your paperback or hardcover</a></li><li><a href="#dpi">What is DPI (dots per inch)?</a>
</li><li><a href="#pixelation">What is pixelation?</a>
</li><li><a href="#low">What is low resolution?</a>
</li><li><a href="#increase">How can I increase image resolution or DPI?</a>
</li><li><a href="#blurry">What if the image says 300 DPI, but it looks blurry or pixelated?</a>
</li><li><a href="#transparencies">What are transparencies and how do I remove them from my file?</a>
</li></ul>
</div></div></div>
<hr>
<a name="tips"></a>
<h3>
Top tips for formatting images in your paperback or hardcover</h3>
<br>
<ul><li><b>Insert images at their original size.</b> Insert images into your file; don't cut and paste. After you insert your images, don't enlarge them because this will decrease the resolution. To insert an image:
<ol><li>Go to the <b>Insert</b> tab.
</li><li>In the Illustrations section, click <b>Pictures</b>.
</li><li>Select the file from your computer and click <b>Insert</b>.</li></ol>
</li><li><b>Check your device settings.</b> Most cameras and scanners offer high-resolution settings. Make sure they're set to high resolution before using them.
</li><li><b>Turn off image compression.</b> To reduce file size, Word is set to compress images. To change the setting:
<ol><li>Go to the <b>File</b> tab and click <b>Options</b>.
</li><li>Under "Advanced," find the "Image Size and Quality" section.
</li><li>Check the <b>Do not compress images in file</b> box.</li></ol>
</li><li><b>Check the image resolution.</b> If you don't know if your images are high resolution, check the image details and calculate the DPI:
<ol><li>Right-click on the image file and select <b>Properties</b>.
</li><li>In the window that opens, click the <b>Details</b> tab.
</li><li>Look for the number of pixels under the "Image" header.
</li><li>Divide the number of pixels by the image size. For example, the pixel count of your image is 1200 x 1800, and the image is 4" x 6". That means your image has 300 DPI.</li></ol></li></ul>
<p></p><br>
<hr>
<a name="dpi"></a>
<h3>What is DPI (dots per inch)?</h3>
<div class="video-wrap"><iframe frameborder="0" height="281" width="500" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/pU7hjmP6fKk?&theme=dark&autohide=2&showinfo=0&rel=0" allowfullscreen="allowfullscreen"></iframe></div>
<b>Video: Why high-resolution images?</b>
<br><br>
Images are made up of dots (pixels). The amount of dots per inch measures the quality or resolution of an image. Images that contain 300 DPI produce the best print quality. As the DPI increases, so does the resolution and print quality, showing more detail in the image. We recommend images at a minimum resolution of 300 DPI. There is no set maximum DPI for images, however, images with excessively high resolutions may result in files timing out during processing, or cause manufacturing delays. The maximum file size for upload is 650MB.<br><br>
<hr>
<a name="pixelation"></a>
<h3>What is pixelation?</h3>
Pixelation occurs when the dots that make up an image are visible to the naked eye. Pixelation can also refer to blurry, grainy, fuzzy, or out-of-focus images.
<br><br><br>
<hr>
<a name="low"></a>
<h3>What is low resolution?</h3>
Any image containing less than 200 DPI.
<br><br><br>
<hr>
<a name="increase"></a>
<h3>How can I increase image resolution or DPI?</h3>To increase the quality of an image, set your camera at a high resolution and retake the photograph. To increase the quality of stock photography, purchase a "print quality" or "commercial quality" image. Manually altering the DPI of an image on your computer may display a higher DPI reading but will not actually increase the quality of the image. Reducing the size at which we print your image can also increase the DPI for printing.
<br><br><br>
<hr>
<a name="blurry"></a>
<h3>What if the image says 300 DPI, but it looks blurry or pixelated?</h3>
Either the DPI was manually altered, or the image is out of focus. If the image's DPI was altered, it will not accurately reflect the resolution because it is not possible to add dots or pixels to an image.
<br><br><br>
<hr>
<a name="transparencies"></a>
<h3>
What are transparencies and how do I remove them from my file?
</h3>
When printed, images with transparencies can look different than they do on-screen. It's common that the transparent areas of the image print with a slightly different color than the surrounding area. 
<br>
<br>
<div class="a-row a-spacing-small">
                <div class="a-column a-span4">
                    <b>On-screen</b>
					<br>

<br><br>

         <div class="a-section a-spacing-large">
            <h2 class="a-spacing-small help-title">
               Set Trim Size, Bleed, and Margins
            </h2>
            <div class="a-section a-spacing-large help-body">
               <div><div><div>This page details how to format your book's trim size and margins, depending on whether your book requires bleed, to ensure your book prints correctly. Without proper sizing, your manuscript may be rejected on upload, or you may see print quality issues with your printed book.<br><br>

<hr>
<a name="top"></a>
<h3>Contents:</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="#trimsize">Trim Size</a></li>
<li><a href="#bleed">Bleed</a><ul>
<li><a href="#bleedhowto">When to choose bleed for your interior</a></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><a href="#margins">Margins</a></li>
<li><a href="#software">Formatting in Microsoft Word or Pages for Mac</a></li></ul>
<hr>
<br>
A few key terms before you start:<br>
<br>
<ul>
<li><b>Trim size</b>. Your printed book's width and height. The most common trim size for books in the US is 6" x 9" (152.4 x 228.6 mm), but you have several other <a href="#trimsizechart">options</a>. Books with a measurement more than 6.12 inches (155.5 mm) or more than 9 inches (228.6 mm) in height are considered large trim sizes.</li>
<li><b>Bleed</b>. Bleed is a printing term that refers to when printed objects on a page, such as images, background color, or graphics, extend past where the publication will be trimmed. Setting your bleed properly ensures printed objects reach all the way to the edge of the page. Accounting for bleed is important, because it prevents a white border from appearing at the edge of the page when the book is trimmed.</li>
<li><b>Margins</b>. Every page has three outside margins (top, bottom, and side) and one inside margin (also called the gutter). Margins ensure your text isn't cut off during manufacturing. Set your trim size before you set your margins, since margin size depends on page count and on whether you have elements that bleed.</li></ul><br>
<hr>
<br>
<a name="trimsize"></a>
<h3>Trim Size</h3><br>
<div class="video-wrap">
<iframe allowfullscreen="allowfullscreen" frameborder="0" width="500" height="281" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/du6Z8K8OsTI?si=niyObvpKYkdlWsIg" sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin">
</iframe><br><br>
You can choose from a variety of trim sizes to set the size of your printed book. The most common trim size for paperbacks in the U.S. is 6 x 9 inches (152.4 x 228.6 mm) and is a regular trim size. The size of your book will determine its page count, and there are minimum and maximum page counts by size, which are listed in the <a href="#trimsizechart">Trim Size Specifications</a> table below.<br>
<br>
	Books with a measurement more than 6.12 inches (155.5 mm) in width or more than 9 inches (228.6 mm) in height are considered large trim sizes and have different printing costs than regular trim sizes. Learn more about printing costs for <a href="/help?topicId=G201834340">paperback</a> and <a href="/help?topicId=GHT976ZKSKUXBB6H">hardcover</a> books.<br>
<br>
<b>Note:</b> To set your trim size, you typically need to adjust the page or paper size setting in your chosen software (for example, Microsoft Word).<br>
<br>
You can <a href="/help?topicId=G201834230">download a Microsoft Word template</a> in the trim size you need with or without sample content.<br>

<a name="bleed"></a><h3>Bleed</h3><br>
<div class="video-wrap">
<iframe allowfullscreen="allowfullscreen" frameborder="0" width="500" height="281" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/ECJYsn5FXsQ?si=SW8C5XyxuFah97f6" sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin">
</iframe><br><br>
Bleed is a printing term that refers to when printed items on a page, such as images or illustrations, reach all the way to the edge of the page. All book covers on KDP require bleed. However, you can choose whether your interior has bleed or not.<br>
<br>
<b>Note:</b> Bleed is only supported for fixed-format files like print-ready PDFs.<br><br>
<hr>
<br>
<table border="0" style="width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; border-style: none;">
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="width: 50%;"><strong>Book interior during file setup:</strong><br>No bleed (left) and with bleed (right)</td>
<td style="width: 50%;"><strong>Book interior after final trim:</strong><br>No bleed (left) and with bleed (right)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="width: 50%;"><img height="305" width="400" alt="Book interior during file setup showing no bleed on left and with bleed on right" src="https://m.media-amazon.com/images/G/01/kindle-publication/interior_bleed_image_setup._CB1573855853_.jpg"></td>
<td style="width: 50%;"><img height="305" width="400" alt="Book interior after final trim showing no bleed on left and with bleed on right" src="https://m.media-amazon.com/images/G/01/kindle-publication/interior_bleed_image_final._CB1573855854_.jpg"></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table><br>
<hr>
<br>
When a book is printed, all pages are trimmed to the selected trim size by cutting 0.125" (3.2 mm) from the top, bottom, and outside edges. In order for objects on your page to reach all the way to the edge of the page, those objects must extend past where the page will be trimmed by 0.125" (3.2 mm). This means you need to increase your page size beyond where it will be trimmed.<br>

<h4>When to choose bleed for your interior</h4><br>
You should include bleed in your interior file if you have any images, backgrounds, or illustrations in your book that you want to reach the edge of the page.<br>
<br>
<b>Note:</b> Even if just one page in your interior requires bleed, then your entire file should be set up with bleed.<br>
<br>
Your paperback manuscript file must be sized correctly for bleed to prevent a white border from appearing at the edge of the page when the book is trimmed. To prevent the white border, increase your page size and ensure that the image extends beyond the trim line. This way, when the book is trimmed to size, the image will reach all the way to the edge. For help calculating your book dimensions, <a href="/help?topicId=G200735480#setup_calculator">try our calculator</a>. Alternatively, use the following formula to calculate your page width and height with bleed:<br>
<br>
<table border="0" cellpadding="1" cellspacing="1" style="width: 75%; border-style: none;">
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>
<p><strong>Inches</strong></p>
</td>
<td></td>
<td>
<p><strong>Centimeters</strong></p>
</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td width="49%">
<p>(Trim height) + (0.125" x 2 (bleed)) = Page height with bleed<br>(Trim width) +(0.125" (bleed)) = Page width with bleed</p>
</td>
<td width="2%"></td>
<td width="49%">
<p>(Trim Height) + (3.2 mm x 2 (bleed)) = Page height with bleed<br>(Trim Width) + (3.2 mm (bleed)) = Page width with bleed</p>
</td>
</tr>
</tbody></table>
<br>
For example, if your trim size is 6 x 9 inches (15.24 x 22.86 cm), set the page size to 6.125 x 9.25 inches (15.54 x 23.46 cm).<br>
<br>

<br>
<hr>
<br><a name="margins"></a>
<h3>Margins</h3><br>
<div class="video-wrap">
<iframe allowfullscreen="allowfullscreen" frameborder="0" width="500" height="281" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/WZ8rEcnkwSo?si=QUYtJXQorTy-wY3q" sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin">
</iframe><br><br>
Margins protect your content from running off the page and being cut off during the manufacturing process. The top, bottom, and outside margins must be a minimum of 0.25 inches  for books without bleed and 0.375 inches (9.6mm) for books with bleed. The inside margin size depends on the page count because the higher the number of pages, the thicker the book will become, which means the inside margin must also increase to allow enough space for the spine.</div><div><br> 
<b>Note:</b> The inside margin is sometimes called the "gutter." Some software programs will have separate fields for both the inside margin and the gutter. Make sure to input the same value for your inside margin and the gutter.<br>

            <h2 class="a-spacing-small help-title">
               Create a Book
            </h2>
            <div class="a-section a-spacing-large help-body">
               <div>KDP’s book setup makes it easy for you to upload, enter, and modify your book before publishing. The information you enter during this setup will be used in creating your book’s Amazon detail page. The detail page is where readers go to buy your book. If you want to sell your book as an eBook, hardcover, and paperback, be sure to create all formats in your KDP account and link them together. <br><br>
<div class="a-span10">
<div class="a-box a-spacing-small a-color-alternate-background">
<div class="a-box-inner">
<b>Note:</b> Before publishing your book, don’t forget to format your manuscript and cover. You can review our guidelines and recommendations on <a href="/help?topicId=G201834190">Paperback Formatting</a>, <a href="/help?topicId=GKYZRXFBZH2LDXAK">Hardcover Formatting</a>, and <a href="/help?topicId=G201723130">eBook Formatting</a> in our Help Center. Hardcover publishing is not supported on kdp.amazon.co.jp. </div></div></div>
<br>
	<h3>Contents</h3>
<p></p>
<ul>
<li><a href="#bookdetails">Enter book details</a></li>
<li><a href="#uploadpreview">Upload and preview book</a></li>
<li><a href="#submissionlimit">New title creation and submission limits</a></li>
<li><a href="#rightspricing">Set rights & pricing</a></li>
<li><a href="#next">What's next?</a></li>
</ul>
<hr>
<a name="topic01"></a>
	<a name="bookdetails"></a>
<h3>Enter book details</h3>
Entering your book details is the first step towards publishing your book. These details directly correlate with what shows up on the Amazon detail page for your book. You have full control over what is displayed. However, keep in mind that some of these fields can't be modified once your book is published. We recommend paying extra close attention to ensure all of these details are correct. 
<br><br>
To see an example of how your book details will show up on your detail page visit J.K. Rowling’s page for <a href="https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0192CTMYG?pf_rd_r=SKJH8EP2752SYNT2HD8R&pf_rd_p=5ae2c7f8-e0c6-4f35-9071-dc3240e894a8&pd_rd_r=992f089e-fe46-458a-a65b-e5417df76292&pd_rd_w=3ZSFT&pd_rd_wg=c0oZo&ref_=pd_gw_unk">Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone</a>. 
<br><br>
To see a list of what details can and can't be changed after publishing, visit our <a href="/help?topicId=G200736410">Update Your Book Details</a> page.
<br><br>
The title, subtitle, author name, series information, and ISBN in your manuscript file must match the details you enter during title setup. Kindle eBooks, paperbacks, and hardcover books are linked automatically if the author name and book title of both editions match exactly. During the publishing process, KDP tries to match book details like title and author name to other editions available in the Amazon catalog.
<br><br>
For low- content books, you can choose to either use your own ISBN or publish without an ISBN. Learn more about <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/help/topic/GGE5T76TWKA85DJM">low-content books</a>.
<br><br>
Entering your book details is the first step of the setup workflow. To begin, follow the steps below:
<ol>
<li>Go to your <a href="https://kdp.amazon.com/bookshelf">Bookshelf</a>.</li>
<li>Click the <b>+ Create</b> button.</li>
<li>Click to choose which type of book to create.</li>
</ol>

When entering your book details, note we cannot accept HTML tags in the title, subtitle, author, contributors, or keywords fields.<br><br><br>
For more specific information, tips, tricks, and recommendations on each detail, use the links below:

<a name="topic02"></a>
	<a name="uploadpreview"></a>
<h3>Upload and preview book</h3>
The next step in the setup workflow is to upload and preview your book. Here, you can upload your manuscript and preview it to see exactly what your book will look like. 
<br><br>
This section of the setup workflow also contains information about your book’s ISBN. You will need a unique ISBN for each format of your book: eBook, paperback, and hardcover. To learn more about obtaining an ISBN for your book, visit our <a href="/help?topicId=G201834170">ISBN</a> page. 
<br><br>
<div class="a-span8">
<div class="a-box a-spacing-small a-color-alternate-background">
<div class="a-box-inner">
<b>Note:</b> <br></div><div class="a-box-inner"><ul><li>If you are publishing a paperback or hardcover book, you will have to enter your print options before previewing. To learn more, visit out <a href="/help?topicId=G201834180">Print Options</a> help page.
</li><li>Ensure the manuscript you upload contains the books interior for the title and description you entered. Your book's description should describe the main plot, theme, or idea of the book. For eBooks, an error message will surface in case there is a mismatch. You'll be able to continue setting up your book after you upload the correct manuscript or go back and edit these book details. <br></li></ul></div></div></div>

<br><br>
<hr>
<a name="topic03"></a>
<a name="submissionlimit"></a>
<h3>New title creation and submission limits</h3>
<p>To help promote a positive experience for all authors and readers, we limit how many new titles per format you can create and how many you can submit for publication each week:</p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>Creation limit:</strong> Up to 2 titles per book format each week.</li>
  <li><strong>Submission limit:</strong> Up to 2 new titles per book format each week, counted the first time you submit a title for publication. This includes titles previously saved as drafts. Updates to titles you've already submitted do not count against the weekly submission limit.</li>
</ul>

<p>These limits are separate from each other, apply separately to each book format (eBook, paperback, and hardcover), and reset every Sunday at 12:00 AM Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).</p>
<hr>
	<a name="rightspricing"></a>
<h3>Set rights & pricing</h3>
The last step in our workflow is the Rights & Pricing section. Here you will set your book’s price, royalty rate, and agree to KDP’s Terms and Conditions before publishing. Your price can be modified at any time after your book is published. 
<br><br>
<div class="a-span6">
<div class="a-box a-spacing-small a-color-alternate-background">
<div class="a-box-inner">
<b>Tip:</b> Click the links and highlighted text you see in the setup workflow for extra tips, information, and guidance.
</div></div></div>
<br><br>
How do I choose the proper royalty rate? Check out our <a href="/help?topicId=G200641280">Price Your Book</a> page for additional information.
<br><br>
<hr>
<a name="topic04"></a>
	<a name="next"></a>
<h3>What's next?</h3>
If you are publishing a paperback or hardcover book, it’s time to start thinking about ordering your proof copies. Ordering a proof is not mandatory, although it gives you the option to see your book in person before publishing. If you order a proof, you can submit your book for publication right away or wait until you’ve received and reviewed the proof. It’s up to you. 
<br><br>
Want to learn more about proof copies? Check out our <a href="/help?topicId=G202131440">Proof Copies</a> help page.</div><div><br></div>
